This position is located in the Office of the Chief Financial Officer, Division of the Controller and reports to the Vice-President (VP) and Controller.

The Division of the Controller is responsible for EXIM's accounting, financial reporting and analysis, financial system support, and servicing of the Bank's loans, guarantees, insurance, and related claims, debt rescheduling programs and certain administrative accounting.

The incumbent serves as the Deputy Controller, with delegated authority from the Vice President & Controller to oversee the day-to-day operations and management of the division. The Deputy oversees and supervises the Accounting Analytics & Reporting, Portfolio Servicing, and Insurance and General Accounting units.

The Deputy Controller provides leadership, direct supervision, and management support over subordinate supervisors.

Also, the incumbent serves as a second-level supervisor to professional and administrative staff; develops and/or implements major planning, evaluation, or monitoring of long/short range operational plans, resource requirements, and/or budgets for the division; and continually monitors and evaluates budget, fiscal, and administrative controls in collaboration with the VP & Controller to manage the division programs and services.

Duties include, but are not limited to: Manages the supervisors of the various Controller Units in developing short-term and long-term work plans and objectives in order to support EXIM's mission and provides final plans and objectives to the VP Controller for concurrence.

Incumbent is also responsible for managing and measuring the achievements under the plans and objectives to ensure success.

Collaborates and influences staff, supervisors, and Directors and Deputies of other Divisions and units of EXIM Bank as well as engaging in interactions with Senior Management on various aspects related to EXIM's loan, guarantee, insurance, claims portfolio program and general administrative accounting, financial audit and financial system matters to ensure the Controller's Division is successful in supporting OCFO business plan and EXIM's organizational mission.

Manages the accounting analysis and recording, financial reporting and audit, and various complex aspects of servicing of EXIM's insurance, loan, guarantee, and claims credit activities such as disbursements of loans, claims, commission payments, and participant shares, processing of premia, fees, repayments, and recoveries.

Systematically reviews operations and changes to Bank programs and policies related to the Division's responsibilities. Recommends and provides detailed specifications for changes to the accounting, reporting and/or transaction systems to incorporate changes in Bank programs and policies.

Presents recommendations to the Controller and the Chief Financial Officer on matters relating to the development of Bank policies, accounting, reporting and/or transaction systems and operating procedures.

Leads subordinate supervisors and staff in the monitoring and reconciliation of various sub-ledger accounts to ensure proper support of general ledger balances.

Leads first-level supervisors and staff accountants in the creation of new reconciliations and strategic approaches to ensure accurate accounting and servicing of EXIM credit and administrative accounting programs. Manages the team on the recording and monitoring of debts owed to the Bank by current and separated employees.

Notifies employees of debts owed, reports unpaid debts to OPM and other appropriate USG entities for collection. Manages the processing of pertinent loan, guarantee, insurance, rescheduling, claim, and administrative expense receipts and disbursements. Ensures credits are properly accounted for in the general ledger and the financial system.

Leads proper system development and performance in order to support EXIM's mission and strategic goals.

Spreedly is the world's leading Open Payments Platform. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Durham, NC, the company gives mid-market and enterprise businesses the infrastructure to connect to any payment gateway, processor, or fraud tool through a single API. The platform is vendor-agnostic by design, meaning customers are never locked into a single provider and never need to rebuild their payments stack to access new capabilities.
The core business problem Spreedly solves is real and costly: global merchants face a fragmented payments ecosystem, where every new market, payment method, or fraud tool typically requires a separate, time-consuming integration. Spreedly eliminates that complexity, enabling companies to route transactions intelligently, secure cardholder data, prevent fraud, and expand into new markets without heavy engineering overhead.

Spreedly is the payment orchestration platform that lets merchants, platforms, and fintechs connect to hundreds of payment services through a single integration. As we modernize our finance systems, recently moving to Rippling and rolling out Ramp later this year, we are hiring a Senior Accountant to help run a lean, highly automated accounting function.
Reporting to the Accounting Manager, this is a broad, hands-on individual contributor role on a small team. Because routine general-ledger and accounts-payable work is increasingly automated, this role is less about manual data entry and more about ownership, judgment, exception handling, and continuous improvement of how we close the books. It is a strong fit for an accountant who is comfortable across the full close, curious about new systems, and eager to put automation and AI tools to work

Assist with the recurring month-end close: prepare and post journal entries, accruals, prepaids, and amortization; complete assigned account reconciliations; and investigate and explain variances.
Perform balance sheet and subledger reconciliations across the general ledger, ensuring items are supported, current, and cleared timely.
Support accounts payable, accounts receivable, and billing in an increasingly automated environment, including review, exception handling, and controls rather than manual invoice entry.
Process and administer company payroll, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and compliance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations.
Record and reconcile payroll-related accounting entries (Rippling) and administer equity/stock (Carta), including related reconciliations and reporting.
Support day-to-day expense management, including reviewing, approving, and reconciling employee expense reports and corporate card transactions (e.g., in Ramp).
Take first pass on revenue recognition: enter and configure customer contracts in NetSuite under ASC 606, preparing schedules for the Controller's review and ownership.
Support the outsourced tax function by gathering schedules and requested documentation for our external provider.
Act as a power user across our finance systems (NetSuite, Rippling, Ramp), helping maintain configurations, troubleshoot, and keep integrations running cleanly.
Identify and implement process improvements: streamline close tasks, build automations, and pilot AI-enabled workflows that reduce manual effort and improve accuracy.
Support the annual audit and maintain clear process documentation for the areas you own.

4+ years of progressive accounting experience, including ownership of month-end close activities.
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
Solid working knowledge of U.S. GAAP, including exposure to revenue recognition under ASC 606.
Hands-on experience with a major ERP; NetSuite strongly preferred.
Strong reconciliation and analytical skills, with high attention to detail and accuracy.
Comfort working in a lean, fast-changing environment where you own outcomes end-to-end.
Genuine curiosity about, and comfort experimenting with, AI tools and new systems, and eagerness to adopt them to work smarter. (You do not need to be an expert; we care about the mindset and aptitude.)

CPA (or active candidate)
Experience in SaaS, technology, or payments/fintech.
Experience using Anthropic's Claude in an accounting context.

Additional Information

Spreedly provides an open payments platform. The platform’s connectivity provides payments performance. Key products and services include:
Connect — A unified API that integrates with hundreds of payment gateways, processors, and alternative payment methods worldwide, including digital wallets. Merchants access the global payments ecosystem through one connection.
Vault — A PCI-compliant secure repository for payment methods. Merchants store card data once and reuse it across any payment service, reducing PCI scope and protecting cardholder data at scale.
Optimize — Workflow-driven routing and retry logic that directs each transaction to the best-performing gateway in real time. On average, 7.9% of failed transactions succeed immediately when retried on a secondary gateway. This is where merchants recover lost revenue and increase authorization success rates.
Protect — A flexible fraud and authentication layer, incorporating advanced fraud tools and 3DS. Following Spreedly's acquisition of Dodgeball in September 2025, fraud orchestration and payment optimization now operate within the same platform.
Resolve — Centralized management and reporting that reduces operational silos, strengthens security, and improves billing control across a merchant's entire payment operation.

Accounting Manager
Counterpart is the first Agentic Insurance™ platform, combining trusted insurance expertise with cutting-edge AI to deliver tailored management and professional liability solutions.

By integrating Agentic Underwriting™, Agentic Broker Services™, Agentic Risk Mitigation™, Agentic Claims Management™, Agentic Coverage™, and Agentic Capacity™ into one powerful platform, Counterpart empowers brokers - and the businesses they serve - to do more with less risk.

Backed by A rated carriers, Counterpart has been recognized by CB Insights as a 2025 “Top 50 Insurtech,” by Great Place to Work, and by Business Insurance as one of its 2025 “Best Places to Work.”
As Accounting Manager, you run the day-to-day financial operations within Agentic Finance - bordereau and premium reconciliation, carrier and claims payments, premium accounts receivable, accounts payable, expense management, financial reporting, audit administration, and tax filings - that keep Counterpart, Agentic Programs™, and Counterpart Insurance Company running.

You own accounts receivable, accounts payable, expense management, and vendor administration outright, and you support the Controller on bordereau, carrier payment operations, audit administration, and financial reporting - with a path to taking ownership of bordereau and carrier payment operations as those processes stabilize.

You build and run the agents that make this execution more efficient as the company scales. You report to the Controller.

Own Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, Expense Management, and Vendor Administration
Own premium accounts receivable from brokers end-to-end - invoicing and installment billing, cash application against policies and endorsements, and aging and collections follow-up - so premium owed to Counterpart is collected on time and applied accurately.
Own the reconciliation of broker premium remittances into the premium trust account, clearing unapplied cash before it ages and escalating past-due balances and write-off candidates to the Controller.
Own execution of Counterpart's spend-management automation - full accounts payable automation, invoice coding, and card-spend policy enforcement.
Own employee expense reimbursement administration, setting the standard for review before sign-off by Controller.
Own vendor records and documentation, including W-9 collection, and manage the relationships behind recurring vendor and brokerage-fee payments.
Own recurring program-level reimbursement invoicing end-to-end, from calculation through submission.
Support Bordereau, Carrier Payment Operations, and Claims Payments
Prepare bordereau assembly and the premium reconciliation process across all carrier and reinsurance relationships, resolving discrepancies before they reach the Controller.
Maintain the carrier payment calendar, prioritizing and resolving issues against each carrier's timing requirements for the Controller's approval.
Prepare monthly loss fund reporting to carrier partners - bank-to-book reconciliation, top-up requests, and check registers - resolving variances directly with carrier contacts.
Execute claims payments from loss fund accounts under the Controller's payment authority, partnering directly with the Claims team on payment timing and exceptions.
Support Audit Administration
Administer the response process for the annual company audit, carrier audit financial requests, and the R&D tax credit - compiling documentation, drafting responses, and managing the deadline calendar, while the Controller leads the auditor and tax-advisor relationships.
Support Counterpart Insurance Company's statutory (STAT) reporting cadence and regulatory filings, providing the underlying data and documentation the Controller needs for CIC's STAT close.
Maintain and continuously improve the accounting due dates calendar.
Support Financial Reporting
Prepare and distribute the recurring carrier partner reporting package - unaudited financials, cash position summaries, and other standard deliverables on a monthly and quarterly basis, for the Controller's review and sign-off.
Partner with the Controller on evaluating and coordinating contractor, vendor, or offshore support for these processes as the accounting function grows.
Drive Agentic Automation Across Accounting Operations
Build and use agents to automate premium receivable cash application, bordereau assembly, premium reconciliation, and claims payment processing.
Feed clean, structured financial data and workflows into Counterpart's Intelligence System.
Decide where agents replace manual work versus where judgment is still required, and partner with the technical platform team to build and continuously improve those workflows.

5-7 years of progressive accounting or finance experience, ideally at a high-growth company; insurance, insurtech, or fintech experience is a plus but not required.
A bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Working knowledge of GAAP and STAT (Statutory Accounting Principles), and comfort operating within a regulated, multi-entity insurance business.
A track record of owning and improving accounting processes end-to-end - not just executing tasks.
Hands-on experience with an accounting system or ERP (QuickBooks, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, or similar) and an AP/spend platform (Ramp, Bill.com, or similar).
A demonstrated track record of using AI tools or agents to redesign reconciliations, payment processing, and routine bookkeeping.
Comfort managing recurring payments, reconciliations, and deadline-driven filings across multiple systems and counterparties - including direct communication with banks, brokers, carriers, tax agencies, and auditors.
High attention to detail and a bias toward getting the numbers right the first time.
Clear written and verbal communication - you can represent Counterpart directly with broker, carrier, and audit contacts.
Progress toward or interest in pursuing a CPA is a plus, not required.

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:
Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.
Hiring manager interview: A conversation with our Accounting Associate Director covering your technical accounting and IFRS experience.
Team panel and Pleo challenge: You'll meet the hiring manager, his manager and a peer from the team. The challenge is presented live in the session, so there's nothing to prepare or send in advance. We're looking at how you handle complexity, new areas and stakeholders.
Final interview: A closing conversation, used where it's helpful for both sides.
Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!
Last time we hired this role, we received a lot of applications but can only interview a finite number of people. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include:
CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light.

What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on.

A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!

We are looking for a Senior Accountant on the Global Intercompany Team to be part of a team that is critical to the company's month-end close process and SOX compliance. In this exciting role, you will support the intercompany accounting operations for assigned regions and work cross-functionally with Finance Engineering and other teams to enhance Uber's internal systems and processes.
We are looking for this individual to act as a cross-functional business partner in the on-shoring and structuring of new legal entities and to support strategic initiatives such as M&A integrations, including the establishment and ongoing support of intercompany operations resulting from those integrations, as well as IP restructurings and tax initiatives.
This role requires an individual with strong knowledge of intercompany accounting and multi-entity structures, as well as a curious and analytical mindset. We are looking for someone who takes initiative, enjoys digging into complex topics, asks the right questions, and is resourceful in finding answers rather than waiting for direction.

The ideal candidate is comfortable navigating ambiguity, investigating issues independently, and proactively identifying solutions and opportunities for improvement.
The ideal candidate will also embrace AI as part of their day-to-day work, continuously exploring how AI and emerging technologies can automate repetitive activities, improve analysis, and create more efficient and scalable accounting processes.
If a fast-moving, constantly evolving environment excites you, this could be an excellent opportunity for you!
What the Candidate Will Do
Own and support key intercompany accounting operations for assigned regions, serving as a primary point of contact for intercompany matters and ensuring accurate and timely execution of related accounting activities.
Actively participate in the monthly close process, including preparation of reports, flux analysis, and balance sheet reconciliations.
Prepare and review intercompany journal entries in accordance with transfer pricing regulations to ensure a timely monthly, quarterly, and year-end close.
Perform FX analysis and clearing for various intercompany transactions, settlements, payments, and collections on behalf.
Be responsible for global monthly intercompany balances across 250+ entities, including the netting process, tripartite settlements for intercompany loans, and follow-up on related queries.
Investigate and resolve elimination issues and review automated intercompany entries coming from various systems to ensure a smooth consolidation process.
Set up complex transfer pricing calculations in iCAN (Intercompany Accounting and Netting, our in-house tool).
Support M&A integrations from an intercompany accounting perspective and help establish and support the resulting intercompany operations, including new entities, intercompany relationships, accounting flows, and related activities.
Participate in strategic accounting projects and initiatives, including IP restructurings, tax initiatives, new revenue standards, and support for new product launches.
Coordinate the review of intercompany agreements with Regional Tax, Legal, and Compliance teams and maintain intercompany relationships in the global intercompany system.
Act as a business partner with the Tax Team on on-shoring entities and changes in tax structures, supporting the implementation of changes relevant to intercompany accounting operations.
Actively explore and adopt AI-enabled solutions as part of day-to-day activities, identifying opportunities to automate manual processes, enhance analysis, and improve the efficiency and scalability of intercompany accounting operations.
Proactively investigate complex or unfamiliar intercompany matters, leveraging available data, systems, documentation, and cross-functional resources to understand root causes and recommend solutions.
Support process improvement initiatives and system implementations, providing intercompany accounting expertise and assisting with the testing and implementation of process and system enhancements.
Perform and maintain assigned internal controls and support critical ad-hoc analysis and projects as needed.
Collaborate with key cross-functional partners, including Finance, Engineering, Tax, Treasury, Legal, Internal Audit, and other teams on a variety of initiatives.
Manage outsourced GBS/accounting support teams where needed.
What the Candidate Will Need
6+ years of relevant accounting experience, with knowledge of intercompany accounting, transfer pricing, consolidation, and accounting in a multi-entity environment.
Strong understanding of fundamental accounting concepts and US GAAP, including foreign currency (FX), intercompany eliminations, and financial reporting requirements in an international environment.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate complex accounting matters, identify root causes, and independently develop potential solutions.
A curious and proactive mindset, with the ability to work independently, navigate ambiguity, prioritize competing responsibilities, and manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.
Strong communication and business partnering skills, with the ability to clearly communicate accounting matters, risks, issues, and status updates to both accounting and cross-functional stakeholders.
Strong attention to detail and proficiency with data analysis tools such as Microsoft Excel; experience with SQL or other data analysis tools is a plus.
Interest in leveraging AI and emerging technologies to improve day-to-day accounting activities, analysis, and operational efficiency.

Experience with Oracle ERP environments and intercompany accounting systems; experience with Oracle Fusion is a plus.
Experience with FCCS (Financial Consolidation and Close) or similar financial consolidation platforms.
Experience supporting ERP implementations, system migrations, testing, or finance transformation initiatives.
Experience working with global intercompany operations, transfer pricing models, or complex legal entity structures.
Experience supporting M&A integrations, entity restructurings, or tax-driven initiatives from an accounting perspective

**Betriebliche Koordination \& Abklärungen**
* Neben deinen Aufgaben im Finanzbereich unterstützt du den Geschäftsführer punktuell bei fachlich\-administrativen und betrieblichen Fragestellungen.
